messages:
sasha: Quick question — we need a concrete SDK surface for paginated endpoints that can resume safely across retries and work across HTTP cursors, gRPC streams, and websocket windows. Prefer something ergonomic per-language. Opinions? :thinking:

chris: Short: expose a tiny opaque resume token + a simple checkpoint API on the iterator. Keep server free to change underlying cursor format.

maya: Agree on opaque token for flexibility. Tradeoff: harder for users who want deterministic offsets for caching/metrics. We should document token stability guarantees.

alex: Python ergonomics note: users expect iterator/async iterator. My sketch:
```python
class ResultsAsyncIter:
    async def __aiter__(self):
        return self
    async def __anext__(self):
        # fetch next page/element
        ...
    def checkpoint(self) -> str:
        """Opaque token representing current resume point"""
        return self._token
```
Checkpoint can be persisted and passed back to client to resume.

chris: TS/JS: async iterable is similar. Two ergonomic options: (1) iterator.checkpoint() like Python, or (2) yield items wrapped: { value, checkpoint? } — option (2) leaks shape into every item. I vote (1).

todd: Go feels awkward with Python style. Idiomatic Go: Next(ctx) (Item, ResumeToken, error) or an iterator struct with Checkpoint() string. I prefer Next + lightweight token return so callers don't need to call extra methods. Example:
```go
item, token, err := iter.Next(ctx)
if err == io.EOF { ... }
// persist token if wanted
```

maya: On retries/dedup: resume tokens + server-side idempotency token is our best combo. Resume token alone is not enough for exactly-once semantics. Recommend: server accepts Optional-Idempotency header + resume token; server will dedupe in small window.

sasha: How do we handle streaming transports (gRPC stream) where state is implicit in the stream offset vs HTTP cursor?

chris: For streaming: serialize stream position into the opaque token (server chooses format). For windowed streams (we slice elements into windows) token points to last-confirmed element. Client semantics: when reconnecting with token, server will start after that element.

alex: Edge cases: partial responses (client consumed N of M in page) — checkpoint should reflect last consumed element, not last received page. Make it explicit in doc.

maya: Also make sure token lifetime is documented (TTL, invalidation on model/rollout changes).

chris: Transport abstraction note: SDK should expose same API across transports. Implementation detail: transports implement a small TransportCursor interface:
```ts
interface TransportCursor {
  fetchAfter(token?: string): Promise<{ items: any[], nextToken?: string }>
}
```
Concrete transports (http/grpc/ws) do translation. That keeps retry/paging logic shared.

todd: Backoff + retry integration: resume token means retries after failure should prefer resume path rather than naive retry-from-start. Also for partial-window retries, prefer resume with idempotency header.

sasha: Ok, proposal for decision record (for follow-up RFC):
- Surface: iterator/async-iter + checkpoint() for Python/TS; Go: Next() returns (Item, Token, error) + iterator.Checkpoint() optional.
- Token: opaque string, server-controlled. SDK must treat as opaque.
- Streaming: server encodes stream offset in token. SDK transport layer normalizes to same TransportCursor interface.
- Retries: client retries should use resume token when available; server supports optional idempotency header to dedupe.
- Docs: clearly state token TTL, partial-page semantics, and language examples.

maya: :+1: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with sketches and code samples per language.

alex: Happy to PR the Python/TS prototypes once RFC lands.

devbot: deploy-bot: note added to eng-platform/arch-rfcs for follow-up task #4321

sasha: Thanks — please add any missing interop test ideas in the RFC (partial-page resume, token corruption, cross-transport resume).
